messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Serving cluster us-west-2 high error rate. Symptoms: repeated CUDA OOMs, container restarts, and IB retransmit spike >18% on rack-05. Pager routed to maria (oncall).

maria (oncall): I'm on it. beginning triage. any immediate customer impact seen?

customer-success: we've had two customers report timeouts and increased latencies on autocomplete endpoints starting ~11:04 UTC. They're seeing 5xx and partial responses.

alan: seeing lots of kernel logs on node gpu-05-02: "NVRM: GPU 0: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 31" and containers restarting.

koji: on the network side, ibstat shows link events on hca1 in rack-05. counters: retries increased, port state stays ACTIVE but sporadic link_down events.

emily (sre): coords: let's isolate whether this is primarily network or GPU memory pressure. if IB retransmits are high we might see stalling --> KV cache growth --> OOM.

maria (oncall): plan: 1) divert traffic away from rack-05 serving pool (canary region/replicas), 2) drain affected pods, 3) capture diagnostics and keep customers posted.

nathan: I'm starting a quick reroute via traffic manager: `trafficctl route set --service=serve-main --exclude-pool=rack-05 --duration=30m`

ops-bot: trafficctl: route update accepted. diverting ~22% of traffic off rack-05 immediately.

alan: grabbing traces. kubectl snippet:
```
kubectl get pods -n serving -l pool=rack-05 -o wide
kubectl logs -n serving gpu-05-02 -c runtime --tail=200
```
logs show repeated: `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory when allocating 1.00 GiB` and then `killed by OOM-killer`

koji: running `ibv_devinfo -v` and `perfquery` on the host. sample output: `PortX: rec_retransmissions=3452, link_down=3, port_state=4`

maria (oncall): @network-team can you confirm whether any recent IB firmware/drv rollouts touched rack-05?

network-team: no recent rollouts. last maintenance window 2 days ago was for metadata switches, not IB HCAs. we'll run internal health probes and check switch logs.

devex: flag — customers using large prompt prefix are most affected (large KV cache). we should consider temporary prompt-length caps per-customer to reduce memory pressure.

emily (sre): good call. For immediate mitigation: 1) enable prefix truncation on the host level for requests routed to degraded nodes (safe short-term), 2) scale up spare capacity in us-west-2 (add dedicated burst nodes), 3) initiate container restarts with carefully throttled backoff.

maria (oncall): executing mitigations: `apictl config set serving.prefix_truncation=true --scope=rack-05` (temp) and `infractl scale pool rack-05 +4 --flavor=gpu-a100`

ops-bot: config updated. scaling requested: 4 nodes. ETA ~6m for provisioning.

alan: while scaling we'll drain the worst offenders. `kubectl drain gpu-05-02 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data` -> draining triggered.

koji: network probe results attached (short snippet):
```
Switch-12: port 5: link flaps: 11:03:45, 11:03:49, 11:04:12
HCA gpu-05-02: tx_err: 812 rx_err: 798 rec_retrans: 3420
```
Looks like bursts coincide with service timeouts.

maria (oncall): @network-team any config changes we can do hot? e.g., alter MTU, disable adaptive routing?

network-team: can try increasing IB timeouts and temporarily disabling ECMP pathing for that rack to reduce reordering, but that needs careful coordination. if we increase `ib_timeout` it will reduce retransmit churn. Suggest: bump to 14 -> test.

emily (sre): I'm nervous about touching pathing mid-traffic. prefer routing traffic away ASAP and then test changes on drained nodes.

maria (oncall): agreed. continue diversion. ops-bot reports traffic offloaded to us-west-2-pool-b and us-east-1 backups.

customer-success: message ready to send to affected customers: short update + mitigation steps?

maria (oncall): please send: "We're investigating intermittent timeouts in us-west-2 affecting autocomplete. We've routed traffic to healthy replicas and provisioning capacity; we'll follow up with ETA and root cause once triage completes." Keep it high-level.

customer-success: draft sent. recipients: staging + 2 paying customers; will expand if impact grows.

alan: after drain, I see memory usage trend: models on affected nodes show KV cache growth ~20% over baseline before OOM spike. quick fix: enable aggressive KV eviction.

devex: config toggle available: `runtime.kv.eviction_policy=aggressive` — safe for short windows, may slightly increase latency for long-context queries but prevents OOM.

maria (oncall): flip eviction policy on rack-05: `apictl set runtime.kv.eviction_policy aggressive --scope=rack-05`

ops-bot: eviction policy updated.

koji: switch logs show no control-plane errors, but IB physical layer saw microbursts correlating with large model checkpoint reloads. hypothesis: heavy mem fragmentation + transient retries -> GPU memory alloc retries -> OOM.

emily (sre): next steps for RCA/workflow: 1) keep traffic diverted until new nodes healthy, 2) capture full `nvidia-smi -q` dumps and dmesg on affected hosts, 3) networking to run controlled `ib_write_bw` tests between hosts to reproduce retransmit pattern, 4) run model repro locally with preloaded KV to try to reproduce memory blowup.

nathan: I've uploaded `nvidia-smi` and runtime dumps to the incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/3791234567/dumps.tar.gz

network-team: starting `ib_write_bw` test, will run across rack-05 spine and report.

koji: while running tests, I saw one node report `gdr driver reset` in dmesg right before container crash — possible interplay with driver version + heavy retries.

maria (oncall): if driver is flaky, plan parallel: keep eviction + truncation on, let new nodes come up, and schedule driver rolling restart on drained hosts once healthy. no immediate customer-facing rollback needed since traffic diverted.

emily (sre): marking incident severity P2 (partial outage) for now. if more customers report errors escalate to P1.

customer-success: current customer replies are appreciative of quick update, no escalation yet.

maria (oncall): handoff note for next oncall: we expect continued monitoring for 4 hours, confirm IB counters return to baseline, verify no repeated CUDA Xid 31 on restarted hosts, follow up with network-team RCA.

alan: adding runbook snippet to thread for followup:
```
- Check /var/log/kern.log for 'NVRM: Xid' entries
- ibv_devinfo -> confirm port counters
- kubectl describe pod <pod> -> check OOMKill reason
- runtime config: kv.eviction_policy, prefix_truncation
- rollback: remove eviction/truncation once stable
```

maria (oncall): tagging @devex to prepare a short customer postmortem template once we have RCA.

devex: will draft. include timeline, mitigations, and recommended config changes for customers (prompt caps + retry/backoff suggestions).

ops-bot: scaling completed: 4 nodes provisioned and joined pool at 11:12 UTC. healthchecks passing.

maria (oncall): starting to shift traffic back in small increments: `trafficctl ramp --to=rack-05 --percent=10 --interval=2m`

ops-bot: ramp accepted. 10% -> 20% -> 40% over next cycles.

koji: IB retransmit rate trending down as nodes warmed and evictions reduced peak memory pressure. no further link_downs reported.

emily (sre): monitoring for 30m. if stable, we'll decommission temporary configs.

maria (oncall): last checks: customers reporting reduced errors. moving to monitoring mode and will file incident postmortem with timeline + RCA (probable cause: transient IB microbursts + driver interaction causing memory alloc retries -> KV growth -> OOM).

customer-success: sending follow-up to customers that errors are reduced and we're investigating root cause.

maria (oncall): handoff to @alan for overnight watch. please include pending actions: network runbook tests, collect driver versions, schedule driver roll on drained hosts.

alan: acknowledged. adding checklist to incident ticket and will pick up in 30m.

incident-bot: Incident (3791234567) moved to monitoring. Severity downgraded to SEV-3.

maria (oncall): thanks everyone. good coordination. :thumbsup:
